goal: Maximize ring-out performance across individual historical opponents and opponents who change their timing in the same bout. Nomophobia is development only. Keep the identity-sealed elite human benchmark separate.
fixed_champions: Freeze every published population, mixed and empirical-game iteration winner and their neural and explicit runners, plus existing matched script ports. Deduplicate only identical executable definitions under shared regulation settings. Retain all names in the alias index. Record unsupported historical policies separately and score them directly in Minecraft.
contenders: Four successive training tournaments compare two-expert feedback selection, a recurrent policy trained end-to-end, and the prior champions. Both experts receive the actual observations and actions throughout each fight. The feedback selector reads current local features, recent opponent movement, our own recoil and observed hurt cues. Two specialist identities are part of its frozen weights. The opponent name, assigned switching time and live opponent inputs are never exposed.
training: Use the original 16 training donors and 8 exposed development donors. For each of four rounds use 64 generations with 32 candidates per track. Draw 12 individual opponents with both seats per generation. Half of the draws target weak historical opponents measured on training donors, one quarter involve fixed or changing expert pairs, and the remainder sample the complete training pool. Train with integer mouse counts. Add each round's top feedback selector and recurrent fighter to the historical field. Publish the actual development winner even when an older entry defends its title.
field: Build switching sparring partners from two frozen experts plus a local trigger, either time since the input loop started or time after the first local outgoing/incoming hurt cue. Include stay-with-opener controls. Reserve disjoint ordered expert pairs and switching schedules before training. Collect independent held-out clocks after freezing the challengers. A switch that never fires is counted in overall outcomes and additionally reported separately.
selection: Rank by the equal-weight mean of the per-opponent average, the average over the five weakest opponents, and the single weakest opponent. Break ties by average then immutable name. Always report individual matchups, both seats, both RTTs and W-tap. Treat confidence intervals and worst matchups from sparse native cells as descriptive. Disclose when every candidate loses to part of the field.
native: Compare the selected generalist, the native selection incumbent and W-tap against all distinct fixed round champions, held-out switching probes, their pure components, and the candidate's weakest five modeled historical matchups. Start each individual opponent with at least both seats and 0/80 ms RTT. Check the whole historical policy directory for additional competitive strategies, preserve each coverage status, and prioritize direct measurements for unsupported legacy opponents. Any broad promotion requires independent native points above W-tap and a head-to-head challenger test. Incomplete cells stay visible.
